record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: For house allocation via exchanges in a social network, determine whether natural exchange mechanisms can be made strategyproof, meaning that applicants cannot benefit by misreporting their preferences or strategic behavior during the exchange process.

evidence.quote: Strategyproofness is another topic worthy of investigation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following setting for house allocation via exchanges over a social network. There is a finite set of agents N = {1, ..., n}, each initially endowed with one indivisible object ("house"), and each having a strict preference order over the set of all houses. The agents are vertices of an undirected social network G = (N, E); a feasible exchange (trade) of houses is permitted only along cycles whose vertices induce a connected subgraph of G (equivalently, exchanges may only occur among agents who are socially connected in the prescribed sense). A mechanism is a function that, given the reported preference profile and the network G, outputs a feasible allocation (a permutation of houses consistent with the network exchange constraint).

A mechanism M is strategyproof if, for every agent i, every preference profile, and every misreport of i's preferences, the house i receives under truthful reporting is weakly preferred (under i's true preferences) to the house i receives under the misreport. 

Question: Does there exist a "natural" exchange mechanism for house allocation over a social network that is strategyproof? More precisely, characterize the class of mechanisms for network-constrained house exchange that simultaneously achieve strategyproofness together with standard desiderata such as individual rationality and Pareto efficiency (or core selection) on the network, and determine the extent to which strategyproofness is compatible with these properties under various assumptions on the network structure G.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has made partial progress: for tree-structured networks with existing tenants, a modified You-Request-My-House-I-Get-Your-Turn mechanism has been shown to be individually rational, strategyproof, and weakly non-wasteful, while it has also been proven that no strategyproof and individually rational mechanism can attain full non-wastefulness even on restricted networks. A general characterization for arbitrary social networks remains open.

status_evidence.title: Strategy-Proof House Allocation with Existing Tenants over Social Networks
status_evidence.snippet: A non-trivial modification of YRMH-IGYT is individually rational, strategy-proof, and weakly non-wasteful on tree-structured social networks; non-wastefulness is unachievable by any strategy-proof and IR mechanism.
status_evidence.claim: Partial positive and impossibility results for strategyproof house exchange over social networks.

status_evidence.title: Online Housing Market
status_evidence.snippet: Extensions consider exchange situations where agents are embedded in a social network with exchanges constrained by network structure.
status_evidence.claim: Active line of research on network-constrained exchange mechanisms and their strategyproofness.
